title: Bring your king closer
objective: Use your king to support a pawn and approach the opposing king safely.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original beginner lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Your pawn is on d4. In an endgame, your king can help it. Move the king beside the pawn so it protects the pawn's square.
steps.detail: A king protects each square next to it. The black king is still several squares away.
steps.coach_prompt: Even this sleepy king can help.

question.prompt: Move your king from c3 to d3 to support the pawn.
hints: The pawn is on d4. Your king can stand one square below it.

tree.feedback: Yes. From d3 your king protects the pawn on d4.
c4 also protects the pawn. For this guided step, try d3.

question.other_legal_move_text: That king move is legal. Try d3 to stand beside your pawn.

steps.explanation: Black's king moved closer. Keep your king active while it protects the pawn. Your king may approach, but it cannot move next to the black king.
steps.detail: Look for a square beside your pawn and closer to the black king. Your pawn still needs support before it can travel far.
steps.coach_prompt: Let's stay close to the pawn.

question.prompt: Move your king closer to the black king while keeping the pawn protected.
hints: Try a square on the fourth row beside the pawn.
Move your king from d3 to c4 or e4.

tree.feedback: Yes. From c4 your king protects d4 and stops the black king stepping onto d5.
Yes. e4 also protects your pawn and brings your king forward safely.
e3 protects the pawn, but it does not bring your king forward. Try a safe square on the fourth row.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal. Look for a fourth-row square that still protects d4.

takeaway: In an endgame, your king can protect a pawn and move toward the action. Keep it out of the opposing king's reach.
